mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds Rate above 5.25% in a given month reduces near-term discount rates, lowering the present value of expected future dividends and equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% in the current month
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than the 30-day moving average of pre-increase periods (t-test p > 0.05), or the discount rate sensitivity (Rank IC) is above 0.05 over the 20-day horizon.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in employment (PAYEMS) exceeding 2,000 after a downward trend signals labor market recovery, which boosts consumer confidence and corporate earnings expectations, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS month-over-month increase > 2,000 for three consecutive months following a downward trend
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not statistically higher than the 30-day moving average of the prior 10 months (t-test p > 0.05), or unemployment rate (UNRATE) does not fall below 3.5% over the same horizon.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both industrial production (INDPRO) and retail sales proxy (HOUST) above their 2023 Q4 averages for two consecutive months indicates accelerating economic demand, which elevates earnings expectations and supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > 101.4 and HOUST > 1307.0 for two consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are not statistically positive relative to the prior 5-day average (t-test p > 0.05), or both INDPRO and HOUST remain below their 2023 Q4 averages for the next 10 days.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 3% in a month coincides with elevated inflation (CPIAUCSL > 325), signaling supply-side stress that reduces corporate profit expectations and produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO month-over-month decline > -3% AND CPIAUCSL > 325 in the same month
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than the 30-day moving average of the prior 60 days (t-test p > 0.05), or INDPRO recovers > 2% in the following 30 days.

mechanism_narrative: Persistent monetary easing (FEDFUNDS < 3.5%) for three consecutive months lowers real interest rates and increases risk appetite, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days in a non-recessionary regime.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 3.5% for three consecutive months and UNRATE < 5%
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not statistically higher than the 60-day historical average in similar policy regimes (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in unemployment benefits claims (PAYEMS) exceeding 180,000 in a month signals labor market weakness that dampens consumer spending and corporate optimism, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS crosses above 180,000 in the current month
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than the prior 20-day average (t-test p > 0.05), or PAYEMS falls below 160,000 in the following 10 days.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent strength in both consumer (HOUST) and industrial (RSAFS) demand proxies rising above their 2023 Q4 medians for two consecutive months predicts a near-term earnings upcycle, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 1310 and RSAFS > 735,000 for two consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are not statistically positive relative to the prior 5-day average (t-test p > 0.05), or either HOUST or RSAFS reverts below their 2023 Q4 median within 7 days.

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 100 (monthly average since 2021) for four consecutive months, without a corresponding drop in CPIAUCSL, suggests persistent supply-side weakness that suppresses earnings expectations and yields negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 100 for four consecutive months AND CPIAUCSL < 330 for the same months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not statistically lower than the 60-day average of the prior 12 months (t-test p > 0.05), or CPIAUCSL rises > 2% in the following quarter.
